questions.q: What does the Feature Store online store keep for each record identifier?
options: Only a hashed copy of the record
Only the record with the latest event time
questions.explain: The online store retains only the latest record per identifier (by event time), designed for low-latency real-time lookups. The offline store keeps all historical records.

questions.q: Which store would you query to build a training set from historical feature values?
questions.explain: The offline store holds the full history in S3 and is intended for exploration, model training and batch inference.

questions.q: Why join labels to features by as-of (event) time instead of using each customer's newest feature values?
options: The newest values do not exist in the offline store
Newest values can include information from after the label date, leaking the future into training
As-of joins are required by S3
questions.explain: A point-in-time join gives each label the feature value that was known on its date, avoiding target leakage.

questions.q: In the boto3 put_record call, in what form are feature values passed?
options: As strings in a ValueAsString field, paired with a FeatureName
questions.explain: PutRecord takes a Record list of FeatureName and ValueAsString pairs; the service uses the feature definitions to interpret the strings.

The endpoint runs on a different instance type than training
The model file is larger than the dataset
questions.explain: Skew is a mismatch between how features are computed for training and for serving. Sharing one feature definition and store reduces it.
